contract: normalizer export contract for the complex supplier: what its program must publish for C1-C3 to become a bank increment
source: research/complex-bank-run3/EXPORT-CONTRACT.md (the prose contract this file makes checkable)
scope: The eleven obligations of obligations.json reduce to one missing artifact: the literal operation program, then the columns, charts, witnesses and envelope re-run on the word it banks. This file names the required exports, their verifiable form, the digest each body must reproduce, and the acceptance tests. verify.py -> check_export_contract resolves every citation below against the pinned bytes, so the contract cannot cite a digest, a count or a status that is not there.

banked_word_export_shape.reading: the one banked word in the pins publishes its physical layer as exact counts, digests and a colouring status: this is the shape E1-E4 must reach on the complex word, and R1's precedent to extend

citations.value: PASS exact actual-chain chart and incidence checks

occurrence_inventory_shape.reading: the bit word's absorbed-occurrences.json is the format precedent for E5: counts per vertex, occurrences as integer tuples per kind, the row identity, and the source pins that tie the inventory to the word it was enumerated on

exact_object_disclaimer.reading: the supplier's flow block disclaims exactness in its own status, so the contract is addressed to the lift/witness pair: a modular flow price is explicitly not acceptable evidence for E3

citations.value: Modular equal-frame flow price, retaining dirty kernel lifts and complete full-frame cleanup. Not an exact supplier certificate.
Exact rational local lifts and inverse gate programs verified; monotone flow and zero-fresh kernel reuse DAG verified.

today.verdict: fail closed: no body export exists in the pins. Every required export is present only as a digest, a count, a status or a path, so the import is refused, the package stays a scheduled target and the kappa keeps its conditional flag.

evidence.value: Exact local invertible flow, exact all-column fresh identity, paid source controls, target read chains, and integer histogram certified. A literal globally renumbered operation program is not exported; dense initial dirty-response subtraction is defined by the exact certified flow.
evidence.reading: E1, E2 and E3 are declared absent as bodies
E1's digest exists; its body does not
E3's body is named by path in the supplier's own workspace, and that path is not in the pins
E2's cache bodies are published as digests only

evidence.value: Constructive exact flow and fixed-boundary proofs; literal globally renumbered program/replay remains a downstream integration task
evidence.reading: the supplier's receipts reserve the literal program as downstream work

required_exports.name: program
required_exports.publishes: the literally renumbered operation program in canonical order: per node its canonical id, operation kind, incoming and outgoing edge ids, and its span

required_exports.name: frames
required_exports.publishes: the bodies behind the three cache digests: frames.json (integer kernel basis per frame with the edge nullity histogram), graph.json (parents, children and the edge structure) and record.json (provenance)

required_exports.name: lift and witness
required_exports.publishes: the exact rational local lifts and inverse gate programs per node, plus the flow witness they were checked against
required_exports.form: JSON/gz bodies, denominators <= 2, coefficients in the six published pairs

required_exports.name: chronology
required_exports.publishes: per vertex the read and write tables: target read chains (nested), source controls at paid-parity frames, and the deferred, side and centre reads with their counts

required_exports.name: children
required_exports.publishes: the per-bin occurrence inventory of the absorbed families, in the shape of the bit word's absorbed-occurrences.json, with each child's frame or chain identity: 1,062 rank-11, 264 rank-16 and 66 rank-20 items per vertex
required_exports.form: JSON: counts_per_vertex, occurrences_per_vertex as integer tuples per kind, row_identity_per_vertex, source_pins

required_exports.name: envelope and integrity
required_exports.publishes: the paid moment envelope in the form arithmetic.py consumes (retained stock, deficit, retained histogram, worst-case bad fraction, fallback), plus the package path, its head, every digest of E1-E5 and the acceptance predicates actually run

acceptance_tests.name: body hashes to the published digest
acceptance_tests.test: every exported body hashes to the digest the certificate already published
acceptance_tests.reject_control: any altered byte fails the hash; a matching hash is evidence of identity, not correctness

acceptance_tests.name: frame-record bijection
acceptance_tests.test: a complete bijection between the supplier's frame ids and the canonical ids, with frames and edge basis values reproduced
acceptance_tests.reject_control: a renumbering that is not a bijection, or an id used twice

acceptance_tests.name: charts and factors
acceptance_tests.test: fraction-free chart inversion and replayed elementary factors on every frame, with the denominator bound
acceptance_tests.reject_control: a factor that does not replay, or a denominator above the published bound

acceptance_tests.name: columns of the modified word
acceptance_tests.test: every source, target and dirty-register column over F2 and over the defining integers, with the target chronology nested and the source controls at paid-parity frames
acceptance_tests.bound: 1320 source columns and 1320 target rows per vertex; read_counts 22/2310/3135
acceptance_tests.reject_control: counts quoted from the certificate instead of coming out of the exported tables

acceptance_tests.name: per-child bijection
acceptance_tests.test: the exported occurrences map onto this package's occurrences66.json items with no other bin touched
acceptance_tests.reject_control: an occurrence outside the ledger's bins, or a block left without its item

acceptance_tests.name: incidence colouring
acceptance_tests.test: colouring of the new incidences with the conflicting assignment rejected

acceptance_tests.name: prime witnesses
acceptance_tests.test: distinct integer Gram/prime witnesses for every frame the new blocks use, residual factors below the retained q bound
acceptance_tests.bound: the retained prime threshold (PR205: 17114 physical roles, all used frames witnessed)
acceptance_tests.reject_control: a repeated witness, or a factor above the bound

not_required: internal id stability: only the canonical renumbering map and the bijection test A2
program text beyond canonical data: E1 is nodes, kinds, edges and spans, not a listing in the supplier's own language
sources for the supplier's own claims: the importer re-runs the columns (A4) and re-charts the frames (A3), so a boolean in contract_checks is a claim to reproduce, not a result
the modular flow price: flow.status disclaims exactness, only the lift/witness pair satisfies E3

any asymptotic interface: general Clifford/tensor, uniform weighted compilation, restored rows, routing, paid layout, prime supply, precision/recovery and fixed tape stay assumptions, so this contract can buy a conditional finite witness and never a theorem

exit_codes.0: admissible: every body present, the gate green and the pinned replay checker passed
exit_codes.1: a check failed: the report names the test, its bound and what was seen
exit_codes.2: refusing: at least one required body is absent, so nothing is run and nothing is certified
exit_codes.3: gate green, replay NOT RUN: no checker was supplied

layers.gate: decidable from the bodies' declared data: hashes (A1), cardinalities (A2, A5), published bounds (A3, A6, A7), bijections (A2's id map, A5 against occurrences66.json) and the counts that must come out of the exported tables rather than the certificate (A4)
layers.replay: the physics: formal columns over F2 and the defining integers, fraction-free chart replay, and the moment envelope re-derived. The harness does not reimplement them and never claims to have run them: the checker whose digest E3 pins must be supplied, and until it is the replay is reported NOT RUN

replay_requirement.checker_source: lift.checker_sha256 of the pinned supplier certificate
replay_requirement.why: the physics is the supplier's own checker, not a reimplementation: an import that supplies the pinned checker by digest may run the replay, and one that does not is reported NOT RUN

import_harness.anchored_digests_are_of_published_bytes: hash files as published, gzip bodies included, and read .gz fields after decompressing
import_harness.self_test: --self-test builds synthetic bodies in a temporary directory, patches the anchored digests to the synthetic hashes and then exercises all seven checks and all four exit codes, so the harness is proven working while the real bodies are absent

failure_semantics.today: 0 of 6 bodies: the import fails closed, the package stays a scheduled target and the kappa keeps its conditional flag
failure_semantics.order_of_discharge: A1-A3 admit E2-E3 and make C1's normalizer a re-assignment over published frames; A4 re-runs C2; A5 closes C5-C7 and the item-to-block half of C1; A6-A7 close C3; E6 closes C4 and R4
failure_semantics.never: no export can make the bound unconditional; see obligations.json -> unconditionality
